summary: [standards] Env leak, not this change's: five unit tests in finding::tests (close_defaults_fixed_to_head_and_refuses_a_rev_on_other_dispositions, close_never_edits_the_record_it_supersedes, close_stages_a_transition_that_preserves_every_content_field, closing_to_the_current_disposition_is_a_no_op_that_stages_nothing, the_current_disposition_is_the_latest_version_not_the_first_read) fail with CANON_ROLE=implementer (cargo nextest run -p canon-cli --lib, 540 passed 5 failed; green without the variable, 545/545). Cause: closing_role reads CANON_ROLE in-process (Role::current) since canon-0-38-finding-closer (79815f634), and the tests close rejected/deferred without declaring a role, so an implementer session is refused FINDING_ROLE_DENIED. The 0.38 test-determinism chore (4a17fad62, an ancestor of 79815f634) could not have caught it: it landed first, and its guard (tests/hermetic_env.rs) scans only tests/*.rs files that start the binary, so in-process unit tests in src/ are outside both the helper and the guard, and its three-environment check was run on a tree that did not hold closing_role. It is a gap in that chore's invariant ('tests do not inherit the caller's role') for unit tests, which the finding-closer review did not run under a declared role. Fix: the five tests set or clear the role they close under (a serialized env guard, or pass the role explicitly), and the guard or a three-environment run covers `--lib`. Blast radius: every in-process unit test that reaches Role::current.
